summary: Today’s pulse tracks Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague, Trump Jr. out as Kalshi advisor after his firm's big investment in Polymarket, and Chris Van Hollen rules out 2028 presidential bid as challenge to take Senate leadership gains support – US politics live. Across BBC, Ars Technica, and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are trump, nvidia, and asylum. In the background, US supreme court agrees to consider Trump’s ban on asylum at US-Mexico border and Walliams allegations prompt calls for staggered age of consent at 16 and 17 keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Nvidia scandal fallout widens as Trump's treasury secretary blames cabinet colleague
headlines.description: Scott Bessent suggests Howard Lutnick’s commerce department failed to ban exports of Nvidia's chips to a firm thought to have links with China.

headlines.title: Trump Jr. out as Kalshi advisor after his firm's big investment in Polymarket
headlines.description: Trump son advised Kalshi and got equity while Trump admin helped Kalshi in lawsuits.

headlines.title: Chris Van Hollen rules out 2028 presidential bid as challenge to take Senate leadership gains support – US politics live
headlines.description: Maryland senator says he wants to focus on Senate’s midterm mandate ‘to answer the call with the American people’ Howard Lutnick under pressure over alleged lack of Nvidia action The longest in the company’s history. My colleagues are covering the latest and how it’s affecting millions and pretty much every industry … As I noted earlier, the calls for Howard Lutnick to appear before lawmakers on Capitol Hill have been answered.

headlines.title: US supreme court agrees to consider Trump’s ban on asylum at US-Mexico border
headlines.description: Trump officials seek to overturn lower court rulings that found executive order banning asylum applications illegal The US supreme court agreed on Friday to consider Donald Trump’s ban on asylum at the US-Mexico border , a pillar of the Republican president’s far-reaching crackdown on immigration. The Trump administration wants to overturn lower court decisions that found the executive order banning asylum applications is illegal.

headlines.title: Walliams allegations prompt calls for staggered age of consent at 16 and 17
headlines.description: Barrister say law does not adequately recognise power imbalance between young people and much older adults Allegations against Russell Brand and, separately, David Walliams have led to calls for greater legal protection for 16- and 17-year-olds from being sexually exploited by older adults. A staggered consent law is one route favoured by campaigners, supported by some Labour MPs. Claire Waxman, the victims’ commissioner for England and Wales, has called for “serious conversations” on the potential for legislative change.

headlines.title: Trump bought up Nvidia stock as he decided on policy that would benefit chipmaker
headlines.description: President purchased up to $5m of stock before revoking Biden-era rule that limited Nvidia’s ability to sell to China Donald Trump bought Nvidia stock worth millions of dollars as he made decisions on America’s China policy that would benefit the chipmaker, an analysis has found . In May 2025, Trump’s administration rescinded a Biden-era rule designed to prevent the most advanced US-made AI chips from being exported to China.

headlinePool.title: Families clear homes of David Walliams books after sexual offence allegations
headlinePool.description: Parents take action while independent bookshops say they had already stopped stocking his titles In Sarah’s house, David Walliams has been a bedtime staple for years. Her children, aged eight, six and four, have dressed up as his characters for World Book Day – they love the over-the-top, unusual names and illustrations. Now, all the books are going. “I’ll probably take them away and replace them with other authors,” says Sarah, a mother in west London. “Sooner rather than later, so they don’t realise.” If any of her children ask why, she will tell them “that his choices aren’t great and that I think we should be reading other books”.

headlinePool.title: Police launch investigation into David Walliams over alleged serious sexual offences
headlinePool.description: Met police say allegations are separate from those made by multiple women in Guardian and ITV investigation The Metropolitan police have launched a criminal investigation into David Walliams over alleged serious sexual offences. Walliams, 55, was accused in reports by ITV and the Guardian this week of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex. He has denied any wrongdoing, being a sexual predator or breaking the law.

headlinePool.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
headlinePool.description: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.

headlinePool.title: The Peruvian city that has embraced Pope Leo as one of its own
headlinePool.description: Pope Leo XIV is in Peru as part of his Latin America tour, just weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

headlinePool.title: Andy Burnham urges Labour to ‘re-arm’ for Kemi Badenoch comeback
headlinePool.description: No 10 sources say PM wants party to refocus on Tories as electoral threat after prioritising Reform and Greens Andy Burnham has instructed the Labour party to “re-arm” to fight the Conservatives at the next election amid concern inside government that they must take the prospect of a Kemi Badenoch-led recovery seriously. Downing Street sources said the prime minister wanted Labour headquarters to refocus on the Tories as an electoral threat after more than two years of prioritising Nigel Farage’s Reform and, on their left flank, the Greens.

headlinePool.title: Labour chief whip tells Vogue she takes tough approach to keeping MPs in line
headlinePool.description: Anneliese Midgley surprises colleagues after Burnham said whips’ office should not be ‘something to be feared’ If Andy Burnham has been accused of being a people pleaser by his critics, the same most certainly cannot be said of his chief whip. “I’m not going to take any shit and I don’t fuck about,” said Anneliese Midgley, the Labour government’s newest head of party discipline, shedding some light on her direct approach to keeping MPs in line.

headlinePool.title: Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook
headlinePool.description: Tech firm says it is ‘deeply sorry’ for disruption and has now addressed the underlying issue Microsoft outage hits UK hospitals, GPs, schools and police Microsoft outage – live updates Microsoft has said it is “deeply sorry” for a widespread outage that caused disruption to millions of users, organisations and businesses across the globe – and that it has “addressed the underlying issue”. The company said the outage was a “technical issue” not related to cyber-attacks or AI agents, and that it continued to gradually restore services.
